hook: Air Intelligence Requirements Memorandum Number 4, dated 15 February 1949, issued by the USAF Directorate of Intelligence under Major General C.P. Cabell, establishing a comprehensive standardized protocol for reporting 'unconventional aircraft and unidentified flying objects, including the so-called Flying Discs' — distributed to the FBI, CIA, Navy, Coast Guard, State Department, and all major Air Commands.
why_it_matters: This memorandum reveals the formal, interagency infrastructure the U.S. government built around UFO reporting by early 1949 — less than two years after the Kenneth Arnold sighting. Wright-Patterson AFB (office MCIAXO-3) is explicitly designated as the central clearinghouse for all reports, foreshadowing its role as the hub of Project Blue Book. The distribution list — spanning CIA, FBI, State Department, Navy, Coast Guard, and overseas Air Attaches — demonstrates that UFO investigation was treated as a serious, whole-of-government intelligence priority, not a fringe concern.
key_findings: Wright-Patterson AFB, Dayton, Ohio (Attn: MCIAXO-3) is designated the primary collection point for all UFO reports from both domestic and overseas commands, as well as non-Air Force agencies including the FBI.
The memo supersedes two earlier Army collection documents from 1948, confirming a formal transfer of UFO investigative primacy from the Army to the Air Force.

Physical evidence collection protocols explicitly require Geiger counter checks on surfaces near UAP contact points to test for radioactivity, and soil sample collection from landing sites — indicating awareness of potential physical trace phenomena.

Observer reliability was to be verified through FBI records, police departments, employers, and neighbors, with interrogators required to assess the 'intelligence and character' of witnesses — reflecting a structured credibility-vetting process.

Radar sighting protocols required tracking target separation (one object becoming multiple), turn radius, speed, and whether radio circuits experienced 'inductions or extra noise' — suggesting known anomalous radar signatures were already anticipated.

legacy_program_connections.reasoning: Wright-Patterson AFB office MCIAXO-3 is explicitly named as the mandatory central collection point for all UAP reports from every U.S. command and non-Air Force agency.
This memo is a direct institutional predecessor to Project Blue Book, establishing the Wright-Patterson-centered reporting and collection framework that Blue Book would inherit and formalize.
The Director of Central Intelligence is explicitly listed on the distribution, confirming CIA was a formal recipient of all UFO intelligence as of 1949.
The memo directs overseas Air Attaches to report UAP data and specifically flags Canadian border activity as requiring cross-checks, indicating early international coordination awareness.
